newsitem.title: CONGO: Violence, no massacres near Zaire town - residents.
newsitem.headline: Violence, no massacres near Zaire town - residents.

text.p: Reports from the remote Zairean river city of Mbandaka speak of violent incidents or clashes after rebels moved in but not of massacres of Rwandan Hutu refugees, sources in contact with the area said.

Both Zairean and foreign residents of Zaire's capital Kinshasa, in radio contact with Mbandaka on Wednesday, said they had no evidence so far to support a claim by France on Tuesday that Tutsis with Laurent Kabila's rebels were killing the Hutus.
"A very reliable source in Mbandaka told us early today there are some violent incidents but no massacres in the town or surrounding area," one of the Kinshasa residents said.
"There were some isolated clashes with pro-government forces but there was no bloodbath," another resident quoted a source as saying.
Mbandaka is about 600 km (375 miles) northeast of Kinshasa and close to the Zaire River border with Congo.
The Kinshasa residents said their sources confirmed that the rebels captured the city on Tuesday.
Paris quoted "reliable" but anonymous sources for the massacre allegation.
The U.N. refugee agency UNCHR expressed concern about the plight of the refugees.
Spokeswoman Pam O'Toole said in Geneva UNHCR had reports from Zairean interior ministry and usually reliable independent sources in Zaire that rebels had killed refugees near Mbandaka.
"We are very concerned about the safety of Rwandan Hutu refugees. We're trying to check out these reports," she said.

Reliable news is at a premium from the interior of Zaire, now mostly under rebel control. The best available information usually comes via the Catholic Church's network of radio links between missions throughout the country.
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) says about 40,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees are gathering south of Mbandaka, in an area of swamps and river inlets, hoping to reach sanctuary in Congo.
Up to 4,000 have crossed in the past few days, the ICRC's delegate in Congo, Boris Michel, told Reuters. He said two light planes flew emergejcy food aid to the refugees on Wednesday.
The Hutus fled into Zaire in July 1994 after a Tutsi victory in Rwanda's civil war and in fear of reprisals for genocide committed earlier that year by some hardline Hutus.
The refugees have walked more than 1,500 km (1,000 miles) across the breadth of Zaire since last October, escaping vengeful Tutsis among Kabila's rebels.
Other humanitarian and religious sources doubt there are 40,000 Hutus in and around Mbandanka. They say many of the group are actually Zaireans displaced by the war. REUTER NK HV njp
